No iOS or macOS app claims the `market:` scheme, so there that branch is the *only* branch: `launchUrl` fails, `openExternalUri` returns false, and both callers show the error toast. The port must resolve the destination per platform — the `market:` deep link where it works, and the same listing over https where it does not, since a browser is always present.

#### feedback.share-sheet-has-no-anchor-on-ipad

- [x] `feedback.share-sheet-has-no-anchor-on-ipad` — Sharing an export passes no origin rect, so every export path fails on iPad with "No app was found to support this action"
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/utils/ViewExtensions.kt:121-137 — showSendFileScreen builds Intent(ACTION_SEND) and hands it to startActivitySafely, which opens the system chooser; no anchor is involved on any Android form factor`

Both callers turn any failure into `activityNotFound`, so with no origin every export path on an iPad ends in "No app was found to support this action" and the exported file is unreachable. The port targets iPad (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2"`), so the sharing seam must carry a non-empty origin rect inside the root view.

#### feedback.csv-target-value-rounds-unlike-java

- [x] `feedback.csv-target-value-rounds-unlike-java` — The CSV export's Target Value column rounds the binary double instead of the shortest decimal, so about half of all x.x5 targets export one step low
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** low
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/models/HabitList.kt:197 — format("%.1f", habit.targetValue)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/models/habit_list.dart — writeCSV, the Target Value column`
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `feedback.csv-target-value-rounds-unlike-java#1` — In the Kotlin app: the column is `format("%.1f", targetValue)`, whose JVM actual is `java.util.Formatter`. It rounds the shortest decimal that round-trips the double — what `Double.toString` prints — HALF_UP, so 0.15 exports as 0.2, 0.35 as 0.4, 0.85 as 0.9, 0.95 as 1.0 and 8.35 as 8.4. Dart's `toStringAsFixed` rounds the exact binary value instead, and 0.15 is stored as 0.1499999999999999944…, so it yields 0.1. The port already carries a Java-compatible `format()` for exactly this reason and must use it here; a target is entered by hand with no digit limit, so x.x5 values are ordinary.

#### feedback.zip-entries-have-no-timestamp

- [x] `feedback.zip-entries-have-no-timestamp` — Exported ZIP entries carry a zeroed MS-DOS timestamp, so extracted files are dated 1979/1980 instead of the export time
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** low
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/platform/io/Zip.kt:49 — zos.putNextEntry(java.util.zip.ZipEntry(name))`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/io/zip.dart — ZipWriter._writeLocalHeader and ._writeCentralHeader`
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `feedback.zip-entries-have-no-timestamp#1` — In the Kotlin app: `ZipEntry(name)` sets no time, so `ZipOutputStream.putNextEntry` stamps it — `if (e.xdostime == -1) e.setTime(System.currentTimeMillis())` — and every CSV inside "Loop Habits CSV <date>.zip" carries the moment of export. The port wrote literal zeros into the last-mod time and date of both the local and the central header, and a zero MS-DOS date encodes month 0 / day 0, which extractors render as 1979-11-30 or 1980-01-01: the files sort to the bottom of a by-date listing and cannot be told apart from an older export. Both copies of the field must agree, and a date outside 1980..2107 has to clamp rather than wrap, as `javaToDosTime` does.

## Domain: Ninth audit pass (2026-08-24)

Six lenses over the port, every finding adjudicated by two independent
skeptics. Three of the seven share one root cause: the port read the locale
MaterialApp *resolved* against its supported list — language-only for all but
five locales — where Kotlin reads `Locale.getDefault()`, the device locale with
its region. The app's UI language still follows the resolved locale; only the
locale-derived data conventions follow the device.


#### audit9.first-weekday-follows-the-device-locale

- [x] `audit9.first-weekday-follows-the-device-locale` — The first day of the week is taken from the app's resolved UI locale instead of the device locale, so en-GB/en-IE weeks start on Sunday and es-MX/fr-CA weeks start on Monday
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/platform/time/JavaDates.kt:50-52 (`return GregorianCalendar(Locale.getDefault()).firstDayOfWeek`), consumed at uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/preferences/Preferences.kt:231 and :236`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/locale_first_weekday.dart:49 and :98 (`firstWeekdayNumberOf`, installed by `FirstWeekdayFromLocale`), with the device locale supplied by uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/device_locale.dart:43 (`deviceLocale`) and mounted at uhabits-flutter/app/lib/main.dart:400`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit9.first-weekday-follows-the-device-locale#1` — In the Kotlin app: `getFirstWeekdayNumberAccordingToLocale()` returns `GregorianCalendar(Locale.getDefault()).firstDayOfWeek` — the first weekday of the DEVICE locale, region included, in the `java.util.Calendar` convention 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday. On a device set to English (United Kingdom) or English (Ireland) that is `Calendar.MONDAY` = 2; on Español (México) or français (Canada) it is `Calendar.SUNDAY` = 1. `Locale.getDefault()` is not the locale the app's strings came from: Android resolves resources separately and falls back to `values/` when it ships no translation for the region, so an en_GB phone shows the plain English strings and still reports en_GB here. `Preferences.firstWeekday` / `firstWeekdayInt` fall back to this number whenever `pref_first_weekday` is unset, and it bucketed every week boundary in HistoryChart, FrequencyChart, ScoreCard, BarCard and TargetCard.

#### audit9.number-popup-follows-the-device-locale

- [x] `audit9.number-popup-follows-the-device-locale` — The numeric entry popup formats and parses the amount with the app-resolved locale's number symbols, so an es-MX/es-US device gets a comma decimal separator, cannot type '.', and saves "1.5" as 15
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/common/dialogs/NumberDialog.kt:60 (`DecimalFormat("#.##").format(originalValue)`), :110-111 (`DecimalFormatSymbols.getInstance().decimalSeparator` → `DigitsKeyListener.getInstance("0123456789$separator")`), :127 (`NumberFormat.getInstance()`)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/common/dialogs/number_dialog.dart:273 (`_localeName = NumberDialog.resolveLocale(DeviceLocale.nameOf(context))`), feeding `formatValue` at :274, `_parser` at :292 and the field's accepted `separator` at :327`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit9.number-popup-follows-the-device-locale#1` — In the Kotlin app: `NumberDialog` prefills the value field with `DecimalFormat("#.##").format(originalValue)`, builds the field's `DigitsKeyListener` alphabet from `DecimalFormatSymbols.getInstance().decimalSeparator`, and parses on save with `NumberFormat.getInstance()`. All three key off `Locale.getDefault()`, the DEVICE locale including its region — not the locale the app's strings resolved to. On Español (México) or Español (Estados Unidos) the decimal separator is `.` and the group separator is `,`, so 1.5 prefills as "1.5", the `.` key is accepted, and "1.5" parses back to 1.5. Reading a region-stripped `es` instead flips both symbols: the field opens on "1,5", the `.` key is filtered out, and any "1.5" that reaches the parser is read as a grouped fifteen and stored ten-fold.

#### audit9.chart-dates-follow-the-device-locale

- [x] `audit9.chart-dates-follow-the-device-locale` — Chart date labels use the app-resolved locale, so an en-GB device shows the US date order on the Best Streaks card

- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/habit_list_model.dart:99-121 (`isSearchActive` on the activity-scoped HabitListModel) and /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/list_habits_menu.dart:88-101 (`ListHabitsMenuState.isSearchActive` getter/setter over the model); the AppBar swap that disposes the toolbar is /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/habit_list_screen.dart:689-699`

1. `audit9.search-bar-survives-selection-mode#1` — In the Kotlin app: `ListHabitsMenu` is `@ActivityScope` — one instance for the whole activity — so its `isSearchActive` field and the expanded `SearchView` in `actionSearchContainer` belong to the activity's options menu, which the contextual action bar only overlays. `ListHabitsSelectionMenu` is an `ActionMode.Callback`: `onCreateActionMode` inflates `R.menu.list_habits_selection` into the ActionMode's own `Menu`, and `onDestroyActionMode` calls nothing but `listController.onSelectionFinished()` — it never calls `invalidateOptionsMenu()`. Even a rebuilt options menu restores it, because `createSearchBar` reads the same `isSearchActive` field and calls `setQuery(behavior.searchQuery, false)`. A habit list narrowed by a search query is therefore never shown without the search bar that holds that query — which is what makes the two-stage X button of `audit7.the-search-bar-s-x-button#1` the user's way out of a filtered list.

## Domain: Tenth audit pass (2026-08-24)

Six fresh lenses — error paths, ordering and re-entrancy, accessibility and
input, preferences and defaults, widgets and external intents, and once more
the tests themselves. Sixteen findings, one refuted, two of them critical: on
any device whose language the app does not translate the whole platform
subsystem started dead and the UI fell back to Afrikaans, and a corrupt
database file left the app stuck on the launch screen forever.


#### audit10.platform-services-start-on-every-device-language

- [x] `audit10.platform-services-start-on-every-device-language` — The reminder scheduler, notification tray and widget publisher are silently dead for the whole session on any device whose language the app does not translate
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/HabitsApplication.kt:76-90 (widgetUpdater, reminderScheduler and notificationTray started unconditionally, then scheduleAll()/updateWidgets() on the task runner) together with uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/notifications/AndroidNotificationTray.kt:101, :107, :113, :124, :155 (context.getString) and :173 (context.resources.getString for the REMINDERS channel name)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart:291 (`final l10n = platformL10n();` inside `_startPlatformServices`, formerly `lookupL10n(PlatformDispatcher.instance.locale)`), with the never-throwing lookup at uhabits-flutter/app/lib/l10n/locale_resolution.dart:101`
- **Severity:** critical

1. `audit10.platform-services-start-on-every-device-language#1` — In the Kotlin app: `HabitsApplication.onCreate` starts the widget updater, the reminder scheduler and the notification tray unconditionally (HabitsApplication.kt:76, :81, :84) and then runs `reminderScheduler.scheduleAll()` and `widgetUpdater.updateWidgets()` on the task runner (:89-90). None of that can depend on the device language: the strings a reminder shows are read at fire time with `context.getString(R.string.yes / no / enter / snooze / default_reminder_question)` and the channel is named with `context.resources.getString(R.string.reminder)`, and Android's resource resolver never fails on an unknown locale — it falls back to `res/values/`. A phone set to Thai, Bengali, Urdu, Malay, Lithuanian, Estonian, Swahili or Khmer therefore gets English notification copy and fully working reminders and home-screen widgets. The port has to manufacture that guarantee: `lookupL10n` throws a `FlutterError` for any language outside the generated list, so the one caller outside the widget tree must go through the same `res/values/` fallback the widget tree uses, and must read the platform locale through `WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher` rather than `PlatformDispatcher.instance` — the singleton is undrivable from a test, which is why nothing caught this.

#### audit10.untranslated-device-language-serves-english

- [x] `audit10.untranslated-device-language-serves-english` — A device language the app does not translate falls back to Afrikaans, the first entry of the generated supportedLocales, instead of English
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:21-23 (the default resource set, opened `<resources xmlns:tools=... tools:ignore="MissingTranslation">`) and uhabits-android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:33 (`android:localeConfig="@xml/locales_config"`, 44 declared languages against 48 `values-*` directories)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/l10n/locale_resolution.dart:62 (`resolveAppLocale`), installed as `localeListResolutionCallback` on both MaterialApps at uhabits-flutter/app/lib/main.dart:55 and :392`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.untranslated-device-language-serves-english#1` — In the Kotlin app: resources are resolved per key against the device's `LocaleList` and fall back to the default `res/values/` set — English — whenever no `values-<lang>` directory matches; `values/strings.xml` opens with `tools:ignore="MissingTranslation"` precisely so that fallback is legal (`platform-glue.localization-inventory#12`). A phone set to Thai, Estonian, Lithuanian, Latvian, Malay, Bengali, Filipino, Kazakh or Swahili therefore runs Loop entirely in English, while `Locale.getDefault()` still reports th/et/lt for the date and number conventions. Flutter has no default resource set: `basicLocaleListResolution`'s last resort is `supportedLocales.first`, and `flutter gen-l10n` emits that list alphabetically by ARB filename, so the port's last resort is `Locale('af')` — an ARB carrying 22 of the template's ~200 messages, which also drags `GlobalMaterialLocalizations` (every date picker, every OK/Cancel label) into Afrikaans. Reordering the generated list is not a remedy, because it is regenerated from the filenames; the app must instead supply a locale resolution callback that answers `Locale('en')` when, and only when, no supported language matches any of the device's preferred locales. Android 7 and later resolve against the whole preferred list, so a second preferred language that IS translated still wins over the fallback, and a device whose language really is Afrikaans still gets Afrikaans.

- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/settings/settings_screen.dart:778 (`_longWeekdayNamesFromSaturday`, feeding the row summary and its picker) and uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/edit/edit_habit_screen.dart:124 (`_weekdayNamesFromSaturday`, feeding the reminder-days label), both now built from `IntlLocalDateFormatter.of(context)``
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `audit10.weekday-name-rows-follow-the-device-locale#1` — In the Kotlin app: `SettingsFragment.updateWeekdayPreference()` builds the `pref_first_weekday` entries and its summary from `JavaLocalDateFormatter(Locale.getDefault()).longWeekdayNames(DayOfWeek.SATURDAY)`, and `WeekdayList.toFormattedString(context)` — the edit-habit "Reminder days" summary — builds the same formatter for both its short and its long names. On a device whose language has no translation the app's strings are English and both sets of weekday names are in the device language. It is also the very formatter `WeekdayPickerDialog` builds, so the reminder-days summary and the picker it opens can never disagree upstream; reading the resolved UI locale in either place makes them disagree within a single pump.

#### audit10.a-corrupt-database-file-recovers

- [x] `audit10.a-corrupt-database-file-recovers` — A corrupt or truncated uhabits.db leaves the app stuck before runApp forever; Android deletes the file and starts empty
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/HabitsDatabaseOpener.kt:31-35 (SQLiteOpenHelper constructed with a null errorHandler, which installs AOSP's DefaultDatabaseErrorHandler), reached lazily through uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/utils/DatabaseUtils.kt:90-93 (openDatabase() = opener!!.writableDatabase) from uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/inject/HabitsApplicationComponent.kt:89`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/app_database.dart (UnreadableDatabaseException, AppDatabase.openAndMigrate, AppDatabase._corruptionOr) and uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart (_initializeDatabase, _quarantine); asserted in app/test/state/app_startup_test.dart '#3b'/'#3c' and app/test/journeys/database_recovery_journey_test.dart`
- **Severity:** critical

1. `audit10.a-corrupt-database-file-recovers#1` — In the Kotlin app: HabitsDatabaseOpener passes a null errorHandler to SQLiteOpenHelper, so AOSP's DefaultDatabaseErrorHandler is installed on the connection. When the file cannot be read as a database — a header that is not SQLite's (SQLITE_NOTADB) or pages that are truncated or malformed (SQLITE_CORRUPT) — the framework raises SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException, SQLiteDatabase.open() catches it, DefaultDatabaseErrorHandler.onCorruption() DELETES the file, and the open is retried with CREATE_IF_NECESSARY; SQLiteOpenHelper then runs onCreate, which stamps user_version 8 and replays migrations 09..25. The user loses every habit, but the app launches on a fresh empty database rather than failing to start. Only those two result codes recover: every other SQLiteException (a locked file, a denied permission, a failing statement) is rethrown by SQLiteOpenHelper.getDatabaseLocked for a writable open and reaches the caller. The port must reach the same outcome, since AppScope.boot() is awaited before runApp and an escaping exception is a permanent blank launch screen. It diverges deliberately in one respect (DEVIATIONS.md): where Android unlinks the unreadable file, the port renames it to `<absolutePath>.invalid`, because that file is the only copy of the user's history and much corruption is partially recoverable.

#### audit10.the-invalid-quarantine-is-the-ports-own

- [x] `audit10.the-invalid-quarantine-is-the-ports-own` — The `.invalid` quarantine for an unsupported database version is the port's own recovery — Kotlin's try/catch cannot fire and the Android app crash-loops
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/HabitsApplication.kt:54-60 (the try/catch) and :73 (`val habitList = component.habitList`, outside it); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/utils/DatabaseUtils.kt:52-58 (initializeDatabase only constructs the opener) and :90-93 (openDatabase() = opener!!.writableDatabase); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/inject/HabitsApplicationComponent.kt:89 and :125; uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/HabitsDatabaseOpener.kt:54 and :70`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart (_initializeDatabase / _quarantine) over uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/app_database.dart (AppDatabase.openAndMigrate); asserted in app/test/state/app_startup_test.dart '#3 an unusable database version is quarantined, not crashed on' and app/test/journeys/database_recovery_journey_test.dart`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.the-invalid-quarantine-is-the-ports-own#1` — In the Kotlin app: DatabaseUtils.initializeDatabase(context) only constructs HabitsDatabaseOpener — an SQLiteOpenHelper, which by contract creates or opens nothing until getWritableDatabase()/getReadableDatabase() — so the `catch (e: UnsupportedDatabaseVersionException)` wrapped around it at HabitsApplication.kt:54-60 has nothing to catch and the `db.renameTo(File(db.absolutePath + ".invalid"))` inside it is dead code. The file is first opened lazily through HabitsApplicationComponent.providedDb when `component.habitList` is touched at HabitsApplication.kt:73, thirteen lines past the catch; HabitsDatabaseOpener.onUpgrade's `if (db.version < 8) throw` and onDowngrade's unconditional throw then escape Application.onCreate, where BaseExceptionHandler has not been installed yet (it is installed in ListHabitsActivity.onCreate, which never runs). A uhabits.db whose user_version is below 8 or above 25 — a downgrade install, an auto-backup restore from a newer phone, a hand-placed file — therefore makes the Android app crash on every launch, with databases/uhabits.db left completely untouched. The refusal itself is parity (persistence.android-opener#4/#5); the recovery is not. The port deliberately diverges (DEVIATIONS.md): it catches the exception, renames the file to `<path>.invalid` and boots onto a fresh empty database, because a crash loop leaves the user with an app that cannot be opened at all, and because the port's boot() runs before runApp so the throw would be a blank window rather than even a crash dialog. Note the port's recovery is silent — only a BugReportLog line — so the quarantined file is not discoverable from inside the app.

#### audit10.every-preference-write-can-throw-out

- [x] `audit10.every-preference-write-can-throw-out` — Every preference write can throw out of the caller; on Android SharedPreferences.apply() never can, so a device out of storage never gets past the port's launch screen
- **Platform:** both · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/preferences/SharedPreferencesStorage.kt:47 (clear) and :65-78 (putBoolean/putInt/putLong/putString/remove), every one of which ends in `sharedPrefs.edit()....apply()`; consumed unconditionally at uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/HabitsApplication.kt:69 (`prefs.lastAppVersion = BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE`), and materialised the same way by `PreferenceManager.setDefaultValues(context, R.xml.preferences, false)` in the storage's init block (:43)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/file_preferences_storage.dart:264-287 (_flush, now guarded by `on FileSystemException`), reached from :211-214 (putString, and through it putBoolean/putInt/putLong/putLongArray), :178-181 (clear), :217-220 (remove) and :62-65 (the constructor's defaults write); the startup caller is uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart:508 inside AppScope.open, awaited by AppScope.boot before runApp (uhabits-flutter/app/lib/main.dart:31-32)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.every-preference-write-can-throw-out#1` — In the Kotlin app: every mutator of `SharedPreferencesStorage` — `clear`, `putBoolean`, `putInt`, `putLong`, `putString`, `remove` — ends in `SharedPreferences.Editor.apply()`, which commits the new value to the in-memory map and hands the XML write to a background thread. The call site is told nothing: a write that cannot reach the disk (a device out of storage) is never reported and never throws. `HabitsApplication.onCreate` therefore runs `prefs.lastAppVersion = BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE` on every single launch with no possibility of failure, and the app still opens on the user's real data; a settings switch flipped on a full device simply applies for this session and is not there after a restart. `PreferenceManager.setDefaultValues(context, R.xml.preferences, false)`, which materialises the XML defaults on a first launch, writes through the same editor and is equally infallible. The port keeps its synchronous temp-file-plus-rename write (durability is stricter than upstream on purpose), but the error contract is upstream's: the in-memory value is updated first and a `FileSystemException` from the write is swallowed, never propagated.

- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/ui/widgets/WidgetBehavior.kt:51-61 (`val entry = habit.originalEntries.get(date)` at :52), delivered one broadcast at a time by uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/WidgetReceiver.kt:77-88`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/widget_toggle_queue.dart:160-198 (`_apply` and its `walked` map) and /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/widget_sync.dart:461-491 (`WidgetBehavior.onToggleRepetitionFrom`)`

1. `audit10.ios-widget-taps-collapse#1` — In the Kotlin app: every tap on a Checkmark widget is its own ACTION_TOGGLE_REPETITION broadcast, and WidgetBehavior.onToggleRepetition re-reads habit.originalEntries.get(date) as its first statement before computing Entry.nextToggleValue. Because the broadcasts are separate deliveries seconds apart, tap 2 reads the value tap 1's CreateRepetitionCommand already wrote, so a run of N taps walks the cycle N steps and produces N separately undoable commands: UNKNOWN -> YES_MANUAL -> NO with the default preferences, UNKNOWN -> YES_MANUAL -> SKIP -> NO with skip enabled. Ticking a habit by mistake and tapping again un-ticks it, from the home screen, without opening the app. The port stages iOS taps and replays the whole run in one pass, where CommandRunner.run returns before the command executes (AsyncDispatcher.dispatch is `Future(() => block())`), so the replay must carry the value forward per habit and day instead of re-reading the model between taps; taps on a different habit or a different day still read the model, because upstream they would have.

1. `audit10.ios-widget-picker-offers-archived#1` — In the Kotlin app: HabitPickerDialog.onCreate builds the list of choices with `for (h in habitList) { if (h.isArchived) continue; if (h.isNumerical and shouldHideNumerical()) continue; if (!h.isNumerical and shouldHideBoolean()) continue; ... }`, so an archived habit can never be chosen for any of the six widgets — the archived clause comes first and applies to the plain picker as well as to BooleanHabitPickerDialog and NumericalHabitPickerDialog. Looking a habit up by id is not filtered: archiving leaves WidgetPreferences untouched and BaseWidgetProvider.getHabitsFromWidgetId resolves its ids with no archived test, so a widget bound before the habit was archived goes on drawing it rather than flipping to the 'habit deleted / not found' card. On iOS the picker is the AppEntity query's suggestedEntities(), so the clause belongs there; and because WidgetKit places a widget before it is configured (upstream's RESULT_CANCELED is unavailable), the port deliberately diverges by rendering an unconfigured widget from the first non-archived eligible habit — a render-time fallback that persists nothing and that must refuse exactly the habits the picker refuses.

- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/home_widget_bridge.dart (`_habitDocument` — `historySeries`, `historyNotes`, `historyDayCount`), /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/views/HistoryChartView.kt (`seriesOf`, `notesOf`), /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/WidgetData.kt (`HabitData.historySeries`, `rolledForward`), /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/ios/HabitsWidget/HistoryWidget.swift (`square(offset:)`, `hasNotes(offset:)`)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.history-home-screen-widget-draws-more#1` — In the Kotlin app: `HistoryWidget.refreshData` builds the card state with `HistoryCardPresenter.buildState(habit, firstWeekday = prefs.firstWeekday, theme = WidgetTheme())` and assigns `historyChart.series = model.series` and `historyChart.notesIndicators = model.notesIndicators`. That presenter builds both from the habit's entire record — `val oldest = habit.computedEntries.getKnown().lastOrNull()?.date ?: today; val entries = habit.computedEntries.getByInterval(oldest, today)` — while `HistoryChart.draw` sizes the grid purely geometrically: `squareSize = round((height - 2*padding) / 8)` and `nColumns = floor((width - 2*padding - weekdayColumnWidth) / squareSize)`, spanning `7 * nColumns` days. So however wide the widget is, every square inside the habit's lifetime is painted from the real record, and `defaultSquare = OFF` covers only the days before the habit existed: a day the user completed three months ago is never drawn in the same low-contrast colour a missed day gets. The port has to publish that series across a process boundary, so the habit document carries `historySeries` (one character per day, newest first, `Square.ordinal` as a digit) and `historyNotes` (the ascending offsets that carry a note), both running back to the oldest known entry, and both renderers draw from those rather than from the sixty-day `entries` window. Deliberate divergence: the published series is capped at 750 days, because unlike Kotlin the port serialises it on every publish for every habit; the widest grid a launcher can produce is 105 columns / 735 days (a full-width ~1280dp landscape strip at the provider's 100dp `minHeight`), so no reachable geometry draws past the cap.

#### audit10.every-command-republishes-the-whole

- [x] `audit10.every-command-republishes-the-whole` — Every command republishes the whole habit catalogue — scores, targets, streaks and weekday frequency recomputed over each habit's entire history — even for a tap that changed one habit
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/WidgetUpdater.kt:81-110 (`onCommandFinished`, `updateWidgets(modifiedHabitId, providerClass)`)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/home_widget_bridge.dart (`publish`, `_beginPublish`, `_habitDocumentFor`, `buildIndexDocument`), driven from /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/widget_sync.dart:184-203`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.every-command-republishes-the-whole#1` — In the Kotlin app: `WidgetUpdater.onCommandFinished` passes `command.habit.id` for a `CreateRepetitionCommand` and null for every other command, and `updateWidgets(modifiedHabitId)` then does one cheap thing per provider — `AppWidgetManager.getInstance(context).getAppWidgetIds(ComponentName(context, providerClass))`, filtered by `widgetPrefs.getHabitIdsFromWidgetId(w).contains(modifiedHabitId)`, then `context.sendBroadcast` of `ACTION_APPWIDGET_UPDATE` with the survivors. It reads no habit and runs no presenter: `HistoryCardPresenter`, `ScoreCardPresenter`, `TargetCardPresenter`, `streaks.getBest` and `computeWeekdayFrequency` all run afterwards, inside the provider, on a background thread, and only for widgets that exist and are bound to that habit. A checkmark tap therefore costs the app the work of exactly the habit it changed, and a command that could have touched anything costs the work of everything. The port publishes JSON documents instead of broadcasting, and its index carries a catalogue of every habit because that is what an iOS widget is configured from (`audit4.ios-the-app-group-is-never#1`) — so it applies the same `modifiedHabitId` filter to the presenter work rather than to the catalogue's contents: a publish that names a modified habit rebuilds that habit's document and reuses the last publish's for the rest, while a publish with a null id — or one where the logical day, the first weekday or the score-bucket preference has moved — rebuilds all of them. What is published is byte-identical either way.

1. `audit10.canvas-drawn-text-stopped-following-the#1` — In the Kotlin app: `NumberButtonView.Drawer` sizes its number paint with `dim(R.dimen.smallTextSize)` and its unit paint with `getDimension(context, R.dimen.smallerTextSize)`, and `HeaderView.Drawer` sizes its date paint with `dim(R.dimen.tinyTextSize)`. All three dimensions are declared in **sp** in res/values/dimens.xml (14sp, 12sp, 10sp), and `Resources.getDimension` resolves a COMPLEX_UNIT_SP value against `DisplayMetrics.scaledDensity` — density times fontScale. So the number and unit label of every measurable habit's row, that cell's SKIP glyph, question mark and fallback zero, and both lines of the weekday/day strip above the list all grow and shrink with Settings > Display > Font size and with the accessibility text-scale slider, together with the check-mark glyph beside them (`audit4.check-mark-cell-glyphs-no-longer#1`). Because `em = pNumber.measureText("m")` is cached in the Drawer's init block under the already-sized paint, the `1.3 * em` gap between a number and its unit, the `0.8 * em` inset of the notes dot, and the header's `-0.25 * em` / `+1.25 * em` baselines all open up with the glyphs rather than leaving them overlapping; `maxUnitsWidth = width * 0.9f` is a fixed pixel width, so a raised font size also trims a long unit sooner. Scope: this rule covers the habit-list screen. The show-habit streak/score/target charts read the same sp dimensions upstream, but the port's chart text already differs from Android at fontScale 1 for reasons the ledger accepted separately (`charts-canvas-theming.theme-tokens#2`, `show-habit.theme-colors#6`, and ScoreChart's `height * 0.06f` being computed on device pixels), so they are deliberately out of this rule.

#### audit10.the-check-mark-grid-cannot-be-reached-or

- [x] `audit10.the-check-mark-grid-cannot-be-reached-or` — The check-mark grid cannot be reached or activated from a hardware keyboard
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/list/views/CheckmarkButtonView.kt:84-86 and .../NumberButtonView.kt (`init { setOnClickListener(this); setOnLongClickListener(this) }`), with `targetSdk = 36` at uhabits-android/build.gradle.kts:57 (android.view.View FOCUSABLE_AUTO, and KeyEvent.isConfirmKey covering DPAD_CENTER, ENTER, NUMPAD_ENTER and SPACE); contrast with .../views/HabitCardListView.kt:126-131, which binds the card with `setOnTouchListener` only`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/entry_panel.dart (`EntryButton`, now Focus + Actions around the CoreView); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/core_view.dart (the bare GestureDetector it wraps)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit10.the-check-mark-grid-cannot-be-reached-or#1` — In the Kotlin app: every cell of the check-mark grid registers `setOnClickListener` / `setOnLongClickListener` in its init block, which sets CLICKABLE; with `targetSdk >= 26` `View.focusable` defaults to FOCUSABLE_AUTO, which resolves to focusable for a clickable view, and neither ButtonPanelView nor the card blocks descendant focus. So on a device driven by a keyboard or D-pad (Chromebook, DeX, tablet plus keyboard) Tab and the arrows walk cell by cell across a habit row, the focused cell shows the platform's default focus highlight (`defaultFocusHighlightEnabled` is true and the cell sets no background of its own), and a confirm key — ENTER, NUMPAD_ENTER, SPACE or DPAD_CENTER — runs `performClick()`, i.e. the same toggle-or-edit branch a tap takes. The habit *row* is the mirror image: `HabitCardListView.bindCardView` attaches only a touch listener, never a click listener, so the card's FOCUSABLE_AUTO resolves to not-focusable and there is no keyboard path to the habit detail screen. Deliberate divergence: the port keeps its row-level InkWell focusable, so Enter on a row opens the detail screen — restoring the cells is what the defect required, and removing the row's focus node would delete a working access path rather than add one. The port also does not reproduce `View.onKeyDown` arming `checkForLongClick` for a held confirm key, so a held ENTER activates instead of long-clicking.

#### audit10.task-runner-progress-before-post

- [x] `audit10.task-runner-progress-before-post` — The task runner fires onPostExecute before the progress callbacks it has already queued, so the habit list is told "refresh finished" against the pre-refresh cache
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/tasks/CoroutineTaskRunner.kt:49-66 (the `scope.launch { activeCount++; ...; withContext(ioDispatcher) { task.doInBackground() }; task.onPostExecute(); activeCount--; ... }` body) and :73-77 (`publishProgress` -> `scope.launch { task.onProgressUpdate(progress) }` on the same scope, i.e. the same main dispatcher); consumed by uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/ui/screens/habits/list/HabitCardListCache.kt:294-334 (RefreshTask.doInBackground publishes progress, onProgressUpdate does the inserts/moves/updates, onPostExecute clears currentFetchTask and calls listener.onRefreshFinished())`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/tasks/task_runner.dart — CoroutineTaskRunner._andThen (the resumption after `_ioDispatcher.dispatch`) and CoroutineTaskRunner.publishProgress; observed through uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/ui/screens/habits/list/habit_card_list_cache.dart:294-346`
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `audit10.task-runner-progress-before-post#1` — In the Kotlin app: `CoroutineTaskRunner` posts `publishProgress` and the continuation of `withContext(ioDispatcher)` to the *same* dispatcher — the main one — and that queue is FIFO. `doInBackground` runs on the io dispatcher and every `publishProgress` it makes is `scope.launch` onto the main queue, so all of those runnables are already queued by the time the background step finishes and `withContext` posts its own resumption behind them. The task therefore always observes: `onPreExecute`, then `doInBackground`, then every `onProgressUpdate` in the order it was published, and only then `onPostExecute`, `activeCount--` and each listener's `onTaskFinished`. For `HabitCardListCache.RefreshTask` that means the inserts, moves, removals and updates that actually write `data` all land before `onRefreshFinished()` — the cache is up to date at the instant it announces that it is, which is what makes `onRefreshFinished` usable as the adapter's "redraw now" signal (`list-habits.card-list-cache#13`). Two consequences for the Dart port, where the mechanism has no direct equivalent: the resumption after the background step must be handed back to the main `Dispatcher` rather than chained with `Future.then`, because `then` schedules a microtask and Dart drains the microtask queue before the next event, so the epilogue would overtake the very progress callbacks it is supposed to follow; and when the background step did not actually suspend (a `doInBackground` that returns without a Future, the `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` wiring `BaseUnitTest` uses), the epilogue must still continue inline on the caller's stack, matching kotlinx's `DispatchedCoroutine.afterResume` bail-out when the caller never suspended — that inline property is what keeps `commandRunner.run(cmd)` synchronous in the ported unit tests.

## Domain: Eleventh audit pass (2026-08-24)

The tenth pass' six lenses re-run over the code it had just fixed, plus a lens
hunting regressions in that very work. Eleven findings, two refuted, one lens
clean — the first sign of convergence in the series. Four of the nine are one
root: the WidgetKit extension recomputes what the app already publishes to it.
One is a regression from the tenth pass' own accessibility fix, and one is a
defect the port manufactured for itself while compensating for a missing hook.


#### audit11.custom-time-snooze-is-erased-by-the-cancel-rearm

- [x] `audit11.custom-time-snooze-is-erased-by-the-cancel-rearm` — "Snooze until <time>" arms an AlarmManager alarm the notification cancel cannot touch
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/ReminderController.kt:63-67 (onSnoozeTimePicked); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/notifications/AndroidNotificationTray.kt:59-63 (removeNotification); uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/ui/NotificationTray.kt:43-47 (cancel)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/ui/notification_tray.dart (ReminderController.onSnoozeTimePicked, ReminderSchedulerApi.snoozeUntil); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/reminders/reminder_scheduler.dart (ReminderScheduler.snoozeUntil); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/flutter_notification_tray.dart (FlutterNotificationTray.removeNotification)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit11.custom-time-snooze-is-erased-by-the-cancel-rearm#1` — In the Kotlin app: picking a custom wall-clock time from the reminder's "Later" picker does exactly two things, in order. `ReminderController.onSnoozeTimePicked(habit, hour, minute)` computes `DateUtils.getUpcomingTimeInMillis(hour, minute)` and calls `reminderScheduler.scheduleAtTime(habit!!, time)`, which files an `AlarmManager` alarm under an `IntentScheduler` `PendingIntent` at that instant; then it calls `notificationTray.cancel(habit)`. The cancel cannot disturb that alarm: `NotificationTray.cancel` calls `SystemTray.removeNotification`, and `AndroidNotificationTray.removeNotification` is `NotificationManagerCompat.cancel(notificationId)` plus `active.remove(notificationId)` and nothing else -- no rescheduling, and nothing written to `WidgetPreferences`. In the dominant case (the translucent `SnoozeDelayPickerActivity` started straight from the notification action, no activity resumed, no command run) no `scheduleAll()` follows, and the reminder does fire at the time the user picked. A port whose alarm and notification are one object under one id must therefore keep the picked instant alive across its own cancel -- the alarm has to still be there afterwards, at the chosen time and not at the habit's ordinary reminder.

#### audit11.reminders-channel-is-created-with-vibration

- [x] `audit11.reminders-channel-is-created-with-vibration` — The REMINDERS channel is created with vibration off
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/notifications/AndroidNotificationTray.kt:168-177 (createAndroidNotificationChannel), with android/app/NotificationChannel.java:309, :319, :320 and :350-353`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/flutter_notification_tray.dart (LocalNotificationsPresenter.remindersChannel, LocalNotificationsPresenter.initialize, LocalNotificationsPresenter.detailsFor, LocalNotificationsChannelCreator.createReminderChannel)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit11.reminders-channel-is-created-with-vibration#1` — In the Kotlin app: `AndroidNotificationTray.createAndroidNotificationChannel` builds the REMINDERS channel with the three-argument constructor -- `NotificationChannel(REMINDERS_CHANNEL_ID, context.resources.getString(R.string.reminder), NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT)` -- and hands it straight to the manager without configuring anything else. In AOSP that constructor assigns only id, name and importance (`NotificationChannel.java:350-353`); every other field keeps its declared default, and `mVibrationEnabled` is declared with no initialiser (`:319`) and is therefore **false**, while `mSound` is `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI` (`:309`), `mShowBadge` is true (`:320`) and `mLights` is false. A habit reminder on Android therefore plays the default notification sound and does not vibrate the phone. Because a channel's sound and vibration are immutable once Android has seen the id -- deleting the channel does not forget them either, since re-creating a deleted id restores its old settings -- this is decided once on first launch, so every site that can create the channel has to agree: a port must pass the equivalent of `enableVibration = false` wherever it creates the channel and wherever a posted notification could create it implicitly.

- **Platform:** ios · **Port risk:** medium

- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/habit_card.dart:187 (`_rowFocusNode`), :204-207 (`_onRowFocusChanged`) and :257-270 (the row `InkWell`, now `focusNode: _rowFocusNode` + `focusColor: Colors.transparent` wrapping a `DecoratedBox` tinted from `hasPrimaryFocus`)`

1. `audit11.focusing-one-check-mark-cell-paints#1` — In the Kotlin app: the default focus highlight is drawn by `View.onDrawForeground` from `mDefaultFocusHighlight` on `isFocused()` — the view's OWN primary focus — never on `hasFocus()`, so a focused child never tints its parent. Each check-mark cell is focusable in its own right (its init block calls `setOnClickListener`, which sets CLICKABLE and resolves FOCUSABLE_AUTO to focusable), while the habit card around it is not focusable at all: `HabitCardListView.bindCardView` attaches only `cardView.setOnTouchListener { _, ev -> detector.onTouchEvent(ev); true }` and never a click listener, so `HabitCardView` is not a Tab/D-pad stop and can never paint a focus highlight. A keyboard or D-pad user walking a habit row therefore sees exactly one 48dp highlight travelling cell by cell across the grid, with the row behind it untouched. Deliberate divergence, continuing `audit10.the-check-mark-grid-cannot-be-reached-or#1`: the port keeps its row-level `InkWell` focusable so Enter on a row opens the detail screen, and paints that row a focus tint of its own — but only while the row itself holds primary focus. Flutter's `InkResponse` drives its focus highlight from the Focus node's `hasFocus`, which is true whenever any descendant holds primary focus, so the stock highlight has to be switched off (`focusColor: Colors.transparent`) and re-painted from `FocusNode.hasPrimaryFocus`; otherwise focusing any cell floods the whole 794px card with `Theme.focusColor` and keeps it flooded for every cell in the row.

#### audit11.long-pressing-a-check-mark-or-number

- [x] `audit11.long-pressing-a-check-mark-or-number` — Long-pressing a check-mark or number cell fires no haptic
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/list/views/CheckmarkButtonView.kt:110-116 and .../NumberButtonView.kt:123-126 (`override fun onLongClick(v: View): Boolean { …; return true }`), plus the inherited /Users/artemefimov/Library/Android/sdk/sources/android-36.1/android/view/View.java:8283-8309 (`performLongClickInternal`) and View.java:32066 (`onLongClickUseDefaultHapticFeedback` defaults to true); contrast View.java:8200-8213 (`performClick`), which plays SoundEffectConstants.CLICK and no haptic`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/entry_panel.dart:95-136 (`performLongPressFeedback`, with `performToggleFeedback` delegating to it), :303-306 and :328 (the numerical cell's long press), :364-367 and :389 (the boolean cell's long press when short toggle is on)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit11.long-pressing-a-check-mark-or-number#1` — In the Kotlin app: every long press inside the check-mark grid buzzes, whatever the listener did with it. `CheckmarkButtonView.onLongClick` and `NumberButtonView.onLongClick` both `return true` unconditionally, and that return value is what arms the framework haptic: `View.performLongClickInternal` runs `handled = listener.onLongClick(this)`, then reads `shouldPerformHapticFeedback = listener.onLongClickUseDefaultHapticFeedback(this)` (whose default implementation returns true, and neither view overrides it), and finally runs `performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.LONG_PRESS)`. So a numerical cell whose long press only calls `onEdit()`, and a boolean cell whose long press only calls `onEdit()` because `pref_short_toggle` is on, both tick — the tactile confirmation that the press landed on the intended cell, before the dialog paints. `CheckmarkButtonView.performToggle`'s own `performHapticFeedback(LONG_PRESS)` is an additional buzz layered on top when the long press happens to be the toggle, not the only source. A short click is NOT haptic: `View.performClick` plays `SoundEffectConstants.CLICK`, a sound effect gated by the system touch-sounds setting, and `NumberButtonView.onClick` only calls `onEdit()`, so a numerical tap answers with no vibration at all. Deliberate divergence: on the default boolean path (short toggle off, long press toggles) Android emits two coincident LONG_PRESS ticks — one from `performToggle`, one from `performLongClickInternal` — and the port emits one, which is the same buzz perceptually.

#### audit12.launch-response-guard-swallows-the-next-tap

- [x] `audit12.launch-response-guard-swallows-the-next-tap` — Every notification response is acted on; nothing is ever de-duplicated
- **Platform:** android-only · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/intents/PendingIntentFactory.kt (showHabit / addCheckmark / removeCheckmark / showNumberPicker / snoozeNotification / dismissNotification); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/notifications/AndroidNotificationTray.kt (buildNotification: setContentIntent/addAction, no setAutoCancel); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/ReminderReceiver.kt (onReceive, ACTION_SNOOZE_REMINDER branch); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/ReminderController.kt (onSnoozePressed)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/reminder_link.dart (ReminderResponseRouter.handleResponse, replayLaunchResponse); armed from /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart (`await responses.replayLaunchResponse(plugin)`)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit12.launch-response-guard-swallows-the-next-tap#1` — In the Kotlin app: every reminder interaction is its own PendingIntent that the system delivers to a component — a body tap starts ShowHabitActivity through pendingIntents.showHabit(habit), "Yes"/"No" broadcast ACTION_ADD_REPETITION / ACTION_REMOVE_REPETITION to WidgetReceiver, "Enter" is an activity intent with ACTION_EDIT, "Later" broadcasts ACTION_SNOOZE_REMINDER to ReminderReceiver, and a swipe broadcasts ACTION_DISMISS_REMINDER. Android delivers each tap exactly once and delivers every tap, whether or not the process was already alive, and the notification is built without setAutoCancel so it stays in the shade after a body tap. Tapping the same notification, or the same action button, twice in a row therefore produces the action twice in a row: two ShowHabitActivity launches, two SnoozeDelayPickerActivity launches, two writes. There is no de-duplication anywhere, and none is needed — the launching interaction reaches the app through the Intent that started the activity and through nothing else. (In flutter_local_notifications 18.0.1 the same is true on both platforms: Android invokes didReceiveNotificationResponse only from onNewIntent, never from onAttachedToActivity, and iOS stores the response in _launchNotificationResponseDict only in the branches where it did not invoke the channel — so a launch-response guard can never catch a duplicate and can only discard a real later tap.)

#### audit12.boot-redelivers-an-elapsed-reminder

- [x] `audit12.boot-redelivers-an-elapsed-reminder` — A reminder missed while the device was off is never shown after the reboot
- **Platform:** android-only · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/ReminderReceiver.kt (Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED branch); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/ReminderController.kt (onBootCompleted); uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/uhabits/core/reminders/ReminderScheduler.kt (schedule/scheduleAll); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/intents/IntentScheduler.kt (schedule)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (the BOOT_COMPLETED receiver) together with /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/ReminderBootReceiver.kt and /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/flutter_alarm_scheduler.dart (FlutterAlarmScheduler._schedule, the Dart copy of the same refusal)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit12.boot-redelivers-an-elapsed-reminder#1` — In the Kotlin app: Android discards every AlarmManager alarm across a reboot, and the only intent-filter ReminderReceiver declares is BOOT_COMPLETED. Receiving it calls ReminderController.onBootCompleted(), whose whole body is reminderScheduler.scheduleAll(); scheduleAll() -> schedule() recomputes each alarm with DateUtils.getUpcomingTimeInMillis(hour, minute), which is in the future by construction, and IntentScheduler.schedule refuses anything left with timestamp < System.currentTimeMillis() ("Ignoring attempt to schedule intent in the past"). A reminder whose instant passed while the phone was off therefore never appears at all: the user simply misses that day's reminder, no notification is posted with a `when` line that has already gone by, no "Yes"/"No"/"Enter" can write to that past day, and the next alarm is the next upcoming occurrence.

A port that recomputes the empty view on every frame must latch on that first notification, or a user who has habits is greeted at every cold start with "You're all done for today!" — the one message in the app that asserts something factually wrong about the user's day, and it stays up for as long as the initial refresh takes.

#### audit12.the-score-widget-s-date-axis-never

- [x] `audit12.the-score-widget-s-date-axis-never` — The Score chart's date axis is two rows — a debounced year row and a month/day row the annual bucket drops — over as many columns as the width fits
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/common/views/ScoreChart.kt:174-193 (footer height and column geometry), :196-233 (`drawFooter`), :288-309 (`maxDayWidth` / `maxMonthWidth`), reached from uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/ScoreWidget.kt `refreshData``
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/views/ScoreChartView.kt (`onDraw`, `maxMonthWidth`); faithful counterpart at /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/ios/HabitsWidget/ScoreWidget.swift:118-127, :235-290`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit12.the-score-widget-s-date-axis-never#1` — In the Kotlin app: `ScoreChart` sizes its columns from the data font — `columnWidth = max(baseSize, maxDayWidth * 1.5f)` then `max(columnWidth, maxMonthWidth * 1.2f)`, where both `maxDayWidth` and `maxMonthWidth` measure the twelve short month names, so the 1.5x factor is the one that ever wins — and then `nColumns = (width / columnWidth).toInt()` and `columnWidth = width / nColumns`, filling whatever width the chart is given with as many buckets as fit rather than a fixed count. `onSizeChanged` reserves `(3 * em)` for the footer, because `drawFooter` draws TWO rows per column: the year at `rect.bottom + em * 2.2f`, printed only when `date.year` differs from `previousYearText`, debounced by `skipYear = 1` after each print, and additionally suppressed for odd years once `bucketSize >= 365`; and a month-or-day line at `rect.bottom + em * 1.2f`, drawn only `if (bucketSize < 365)` — the month's short name the first time a month appears and the day number afterwards. With the detail screen's spinner on "Year" the second row is therefore never drawn at all and the axis reads 2026, 2024, 2022; at every other bucket both rows are present. A widget chart with no year branch labels an annual series with month abbreviations and repeated day numbers, and one pinned to six columns hides history the same widget shows upstream.

- **Severity:** major

1. `audit12.coloraccent-never-reaches-the-text-input#1` — In the Kotlin app: `AppBaseTheme` and `AppBaseThemeDark` both declare `<item name="colorAccent">?aboutScreenColor</item>` — `@color/blue_800` (#1565C0) in the light theme and `@color/blue_300` (#64B5F6) in the dark one, which `AppBaseThemeDark.PureBlack` inherits because it restates neither. AppCompat resolves `colorControlActivated` from `colorAccent`, and the platform text-input chrome is tinted from it: `textCursorDrawable` is `text_cursor_material`, whose `android:tint` is `?attr/colorControlActivated`, and the `abc_text_select_handle_left/right/middle` drawables are tinted the same way. `@style/FormInput`, which the edit-habit fields use, overrides only `android:background` (to `@color/transparent`, so there is no underline) and leaves the cursor and the handles on the theme. So every text field in the app draws a saturated accent caret and accent selection handles — the habit name, question, unit, target and notes fields, the number and check-mark popups, the `EditTextPreference` dialogs in Settings, and the toolbar `SearchView` — and it is the same blue the About card headers and the Settings category headers use, so the screens read as one palette. A port that leaves these on a framework default derived from its primary colour puts an invisible caret in the autofocused number keypad in both dark themes and in the toolbar search field in all three.

#### audit12.the-date-strip-and-subtitle-card-read

So with "Use pure black background" on, both surfaces are #000000 like every other surface on screen. A port that points these two surfaces at the token instead of the attribute is right in the light and dark themes by coincidence and wrong under pure black, where the whole point of the setting is that black pixels stay off.

## Domain: Thirteenth audit pass (2026-08-24)

The same seven lenses over the code the twelfth pass fixed. One finding
confirmed, two refuted — 16, then 11, then 6, then 1.

#### audit13.a-snooze-overtaken-by-completion-moves

- [x] `audit13.a-snooze-overtaken-by-completion-moves` — A snoozed reminder that the user completes before the snooze fires moves the next day's reminder to the snoozed hour
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/uhabits/core/reminders/ReminderScheduler.kt (schedule's snooze branch; onCommandFinished's `if (command is CreateRepetitionCommand) return`) with uhabits-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/core/ui/NotificationTray.kt (ShowNotificationTask.onPostExecute, gate 1) and uhabits-android/.../receivers/ReminderController.kt (onShowReminder)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/flutter_alarm_scheduler.dart — FlutterAlarmScheduler._advanceToReminderDay`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit13.a-snooze-overtaken-by-completion-moves#1` — In the Kotlin app: a snoozed instant is only ever an alarm time, never a template for later days. `ReminderScheduler.schedule` substitutes `snoozedUntil` for `getUpcomingTimeInMillis(hour, minute)` while it is still in the future, and nothing advances it: ticking the habit off runs `CreateRepetitionCommand`, which `onCommandFinished` explicitly returns on, so the alarm stays where it was. At the snoozed instant the alarm fires, gate 1 of `ShowNotificationTask` drops the notification because the habit is already complete, and `onShowReminder`'s trailing `scheduleAll()` — now seeing an expired snooze — clears it and re-arms from the habit's own reminder time. The next day's reminder is therefore at the hour the user configured. The port has no fire-time hook, so gate 1 lives in the scheduler and a rejected day is skipped before the alarm is filed; the day-stepping must therefore rebase each later day on the habit's own reminder time rather than adding whole days to the instant it was handed, which while a snooze is live is the snoozed one.

## Domain: Fourteenth audit pass (2026-08-24)

Three findings, two of them the same critical regression reported independently
by two lenses: the day-stepping added by the thirteenth pass derived its base
day from a UTC instant, and every reminder test in the suite pins GMT — the one
offset at which that is indistinguishable from correct.

#### audit14.day-stepping-derives-its-base-day-from-utc

- [x] `audit14.day-stepping-derives-its-base-day-from-utc` — The reminder day-stepping derives the reminder's own day from a UTC instant, so every skipped day lands on the wrong date outside GMT
- **Platform:** core · **Port risk:** high
- **Source:** `uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/uhabits/core/reminders/ReminderScheduler.kt (schedule/scheduleAtTime) with uhabits-core/src/jvmMain/java/org/isoron/platform/time/DateUtils.kt:78-97 (getUpcomingTimeInMillis ends in applyTimezone, i.e. a UTC instant)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/flutter_alarm_scheduler.dart — FlutterAlarmScheduler._advanceToReminderDay, the `ownDay` derivation`
- **Severity:** critical

1. `audit14.day-stepping-derives-its-base-day-from-utc#1` — In the Kotlin app: no day arithmetic is ever done on a reminder instant. Every firing ends in `ReminderController.onShowReminder`'s `scheduleAll()`, which re-derives the next instant from the habit's wall-clock `hour:minute` through `getUpcomingTimeInMillis`, so the reminder is on the correct local day in every timezone. The port has no fire-time hook and must therefore step over rejected days at schedule time — and the day a reminder instant belongs to is its LOCAL day. `getUpcomingTimeInMillis` returns a UTC instant while `LocalDate.fromUnixTime` is a plain floor-divide that wants timezone-removed local millis, which is what the neighbouring `LocalDate.fromUnixTime(timestamp)` receives. Mixing the two agrees only at GMT: west of it (reminder hour + |offset| >= 24) every stepped-to day lands a day early, east of it (reminder hour < offset) a day late. Concretely, a completed habit in New York still buzzes at its own evening reminder and a "Yes" tap writes the checkmark to tomorrow, and a Mon/Wed/Fri reminder in Tokyo arrives on Thursday. The conversion has to be applied before the day is taken.

#### audit14.selection-bar-keeps-the-toolbar-colour

- [x] `audit14.selection-bar-keeps-the-toolbar-colour` — The selection-mode contextual bar is painted the toolbar colour instead of ?attr/actionModeBackground, so entering selection mode changes nothing about the bar
- **Platform:** ui · **Port risk:** low
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/res/values/styles.xml:24 (actionModeBackground = @color/grey_700 in AppBaseTheme) and :72 (@color/grey_800 in AppBaseThemeDark), resolved by androidx.appcompat's Widget.AppCompat.ActionMode on the bar ListHabitsSelectionMenu.startSelection inflates`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/gui/theme.dart (actionModeBackgroundColor) and uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/habit_list_screen.dart, where the selection menu is built`
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `audit14.selection-bar-keeps-the-toolbar-colour#1` — In the Kotlin app: `startSupportActionMode` inflates the contextual bar with `style="?attr/actionModeStyle"`, whose background is `?attr/actionModeBackground` — `@color/grey_700` (#616161) in the light theme and `@color/grey_800` (#424242) in the dark one, which `AppBaseThemeDark.PureBlack` inherits by restating neither. Long-pressing a habit therefore recolours the top bar to a grey that is visibly not the toolbar's, and the colour returns when the selection ends. That recolouring is the standard Android cue that a contextual bar has taken the screen over; without it the only signal is that the title becomes a number.

## Domain: Fifteenth audit pass (2026-08-24)

Eight lenses — the seven of the previous passes plus a new one for timezones
and the day boundary, added because the fourteenth pass found a regression the
GMT-pinned suite could not see. Four lenses came back clean. The timezone lens
found not an offset bug but a day-boundary one: the iOS widgets never rolled
over at all, the Android half of that same rule having been fixed by the sixth
pass without its iOS counterpart ever being written.


#### audit15.ios-home-screen-widgets-never-roll

- [x] `audit15.ios-home-screen-widgets-never-roll` — A home-screen widget draws the day the user is on, and the tap it sends lands on that day
- **Platform:** ios · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/CheckmarkWidget.kt:44,52-63 (refreshData calls getToday(), showNumberPicker(habit, getToday())); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/WidgetUpdater.kt (scheduleStartDayWidgetUpdate → getStartOfTomorrowWithOffset(midnightDelayHours, 0)); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/receivers/WidgetReceiver.kt:106-109 (ACTION_UPDATE_WIDGETS_VALUE → setToday(computeToday(prefs.midnightDelayHours, 0)) + updateWidgets()); uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/intents/IntentParser.kt (parseDate: defaults the 'timestamp' extra to getToday().unixTime and throws IllegalArgumentException("timestamp is not valid") for anything later)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/ios/HabitsWidget/WidgetData.swift (WidgetStore.logicalToday / startOfNextDay / daysSince / rolledDocument / rolledForward / rolledHabit; WidgetIndex.midnightDelayHours; WidgetStore.stageToggle); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/ios/HabitsWidget/HabitTimeline.swift (timeline reload policy, entry(for:)); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/home_widget_bridge.dart:buildIndexDocument ('midnightDelayHours'); /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/widget_toggle_queue.dart:_apply; mirrors /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/isoron/uhabits/widgets/WidgetData.kt:139,240`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit15.ios-home-screen-widgets-never-roll#1` — In the Kotlin app: a widget redraws from live app state, so it can never draw a day that has already passed. `CheckmarkWidget.refreshData` calls `getToday()` on every ACTION_APPWIDGET_UPDATE and reads `habit.computedEntries.get(today)` and `habit.scores[today]` out of the database, and `pendingIntentFactory.showNumberPicker(habit, getToday())` rebuilds the value-picker intent against that same fresh day. The app-wide `getToday()` is re-stamped without the app being opened: `WidgetUpdater.scheduleStartDayWidgetUpdate()` arms an AlarmManager RTC broadcast at `getStartOfTomorrowWithOffset(midnightDelayHours, 0)`, and `WidgetReceiver`'s ACTION_UPDATE_WIDGETS_VALUE branch runs `setToday(computeToday(prefs.midnightDelayHours, 0))` and redraws every widget. The tap carries no day at all: an ACTION_TOGGLE_REPETITION broadcast has no `timestamp` extra, so `IntentParser.parseDate` supplies `getToday().unixTime` in its place and throws IllegalArgumentException("timestamp is not valid") for a stamp later than that — which `WidgetReceiver.onReceive` catches, leaving the broadcast unhandled. A Checkmark widget left on the home screen therefore shows the new day unchecked at the user's own midnight, the History grid's last column and the Score ring move with it, and a tap on it always records against the day the app is on. (Where a port ships the widget data as a published snapshot instead, the host that redraws it has to advance the snapshot itself: the day is re-stamped and every newest-first array — entries, the entry value, the note flags, the History series and its note offsets — shifts by the whole days that have passed, while the whole-history reductions `score`, `scores`, `streaks`, `weekdayFrequency` and `targetRows` legitimately ride along stale until the app republishes.)

#### audit15.the-notification-permission-prompt-is-never

- [x] `audit15.the-notification-permission-prompt-is-never` — Finishing the habit editor resumes the habit list, and that resume is what asks for the notification permission
- **Platform:** both · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/list/ListHabitsActivity.kt:114-152 (onResume: `if (appComponent.reminderScheduler.hasHabitsWithReminders()) { if (SDK_INT < TIRAMISU) scheduleReminders() else if (checkSelfPermission(this, POST_NOTIFICATIONS) == PERMISSION_GRANTED) scheduleReminders() else if (!permissionAlreadyRequested) { permissionLauncher.launch(POST_NOTIFICATIONS); permissionAlreadyRequested = true } }`, with `permissionAlreadyRequested` a field of the activity and `scheduleReminders()` = `appComponent.reminderScheduler.scheduleAll()`); reached after EditHabitActivity, SettingsActivity or ShowHabitActivity finishes`
- **Where the port should do it:** `/Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/list/habit_list_screen.dart:423-460 (`didPopNext` -> `_runPermissionGate()`), sharing the one gate built by /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/state/app_scope.dart:494-521 (`AppScope.reminderPermissionGate`) with /Users/artemefimov/Desktop/uhabits/uhabits-flutter/app/lib/main.dart:291 (`_ThemedAppState._onResume`)`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit15.the-notification-permission-prompt-is-never#1` — In the Kotlin app: the POST_NOTIFICATIONS block is part of `ListHabitsActivity.onResume`, so it runs on every resume of the list activity — and finishing `EditHabitActivity`, `SettingsActivity` or `ShowHabitActivity` is a resume, not only a return from the background. On a fresh install the sequence is: launch with no habits, so `reminderScheduler.hasHabitsWithReminders()` is false and nothing is asked; create the first habit with a reminder in the editor and press Save; the editor finishes, `ListHabitsActivity.onResume` runs immediately, `hasHabitsWithReminders()` is now true, the permission is not granted and `permissionAlreadyRequested` is false, so `permissionLauncher.launch(POST_NOTIFICATIONS)` fires right there — before the user has left the app — and the grant runs `scheduleReminders()` = `reminderScheduler.scheduleAll()`, so the reminder just configured is armed in time to fire. The block is unconditional on which activity was on top, unlike anything the list does on its own pause. `permissionAlreadyRequested` is a field of the activity and `EditHabitActivity` does not destroy `ListHabitsActivity`, so the flag survives the editor round trip: a user who taps Deny is asked once per launch and not again on the next return, which is the infinite onResume loop the upstream comment warns about. A user with no habit carrying a reminder is never shown the system dialog, on a return from the editor no more than on a launch.

#### audit15.subtitle-card-frequency-and-off-are-hard-coded

- [x] `audit15.subtitle-card-frequency-and-off-are-hard-coded` — The Show-habit subtitle card prints the frequency sentence and the reminder "Off" in hard-coded English in all 47 languages
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/show/views/SubtitleCardView.kt:50-62 (setState → frequencyLabel / reminderLabel) · uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/edit/EditHabitActivity.kt:62-70 (formatFrequency(freqNum, freqDen, resources)) · uhabits-android/src/main/res/values-ru-rRU/strings.xml:65 (reminder_off), :126 (every_day)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/show/cards/subtitle_card_view.dart:141-149 (the frequency label) and :173-186 (`_reminderText`), which now call the shared `formatFrequency(num, den, l10n)` from uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/edit/edit_habit_screen.dart:60 and `l10n.reminderOff`; the English literals are gone from uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/ui/screens/habits/show/views/subtitle_card.dart`
- **Severity:** major

1. `audit15.subtitle-card-frequency-and-off-are-hard-coded#1` — In the Kotlin app: `SubtitleCardView.setState` builds both of its remaining labels from `Resources`, not from the KMP state object. The frequency label is `formatFrequency(state.frequency.numerator, state.frequency.denominator, resources)` — the top-level function in EditHabitActivity.kt that SubtitleCardView.kt imports outright — and every one of its seven branches is a `resources.getString` call: `R.string.every_month`, `x_times_per_month`, `every_day`, `every_week`, `every_x_days`, `x_times_per_week`, `x_times_per_y_days`. When `state.reminder` is null the reminder label is `resources.getString(R.string.reminder_off)`. All eight strings ship translated in the 43 `values-<lang>/strings.xml` directories, so on a Russian phone the subtitle row reads "Каждый день" and "Выкл" and on a German one "Monatlich" and "Aus". The branch ORDER is what makes 1/30 read "Every month" rather than "1 times per month" and 7/7 — normalised to 1/1 by Frequency — read "Every day"; the order is the rule, the English wording is only the `values/` fallback. Because Kotlin reuses one `formatFrequency`, the Show screen and the Edit screen can never print different sentences for the same habit.

#### audit15.subtitle-card-reminder-time-ignores-the-device-locale

- [x] `audit15.subtitle-card-reminder-time-ignores-the-device-locale` — The subtitle card's reminder time is always the en-US 12-hour pattern, ignoring the device locale's time format
- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium
- **Source:** `uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/activities/habits/show/views/SubtitleCardView.kt:58-62 · uhabits-android/src/main/java/org/isoron/uhabits/utils/DateExtensions.kt:62-68 (formatTime → DateFormat.getTimeFormat(context), TimeZone forced to UTC)`
- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/platform/device_time_format.dart:47-68 (`formatDeviceTime`, the pattern half, reading `DeviceLocale.nameOf(context)` through `resolveDateLocaleName`), consumed by uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/show/cards/subtitle_card_view.dart:175-186; the clock wrap stays at uhabits-flutter/packages/uhabits_core/lib/src/ui/screens/habits/show/views/subtitle_card.dart:108-113 (`SubtitleCardState.minuteOfDay`)`
- **Severity:** cosmetic

1. `audit15.subtitle-card-reminder-time-ignores-the-device-locale#1` — In the Kotlin app: a set reminder is rendered by `formatTime(context, reminder.hour, reminder.minute)`, which builds a `Date` from `(hours * 60 + minutes) * 60 * 1000L`, formats it with `android.text.format.DateFormat.getTimeFormat(context)` and forces the formatter's `TimeZone` to UTC — so the clock wraps modulo a day (hour 25 prints as 01:00) and no time zone can shift it. `getTimeFormat` is `new SimpleDateFormat(LocaleData.get(locale).timeFormat_hm_or_Hm, locale)` where `locale` is `context.getResources().getConfiguration().locale`: ICU's best pattern for the "hm" or "Hm" skeleton, chosen by `DateFormat.is24HourFormat(context)`, in the DEVICE locale with its region — the same `Locale.getDefault()`-shaped split `audit9.chart-dates-follow-the-device-locale#1` and `audit10.weekday-name-rows-follow-the-device-locale#1` record, never the locale the app's strings resolved to. A Korean phone therefore shows "오전 8:30", an en-AU one "8:30 am" while its strings are the plain English `values/` ones, an fr-CA one "08 h 30" under a 24-hour setting; only en-US gives "8:30 AM". The 12/24 switch is the system setting, the pattern is the device locale, and the app's UI language is neither.

- **Platform:** android · **Port risk:** medium

- **Where the port should do it:** `uhabits-flutter/app/lib/ui/habits/edit/edit_habit_screen.dart:1158-1180 (`_HabitTypeCard.build`), with the four numbers at :1085-1104 (`HabitTypeDialog.cardBorderRadius`, `cardStrokeWidth`, `cardRippleHighlightOpacity`)`

1. `audit15.habit-type-cards-lose-their-2dp-outline#1` — In the Kotlin app: both cards of the habit-type chooser carry `style="@style/SelectHabitTypeButton"`, whose `android:background` is `@drawable/round_ripple` — a `<ripple android:color="?colorAccent">` wrapping a rectangle with `<solid android:color="?cardBgColor"/>`, `<stroke android:width="2dp" android:color="?android:textColor"/>` and `<corners android:radius="5dp"/>`. The dialog's `R.style.Translucent` theme is layered over the activity theme by ContextThemeWrapper, so all three attributes resolve per app theme: the fill is `?cardBgColor` — #FAFAFA light, #303030 dark, #000000 pure black — and the stroke is `?android:textColor` — #424242 light, #F5F5F5 dark, #EEEEEE pure black. That 2dp near-white stroke is the whole of each card's shape against the #a0000000 scrim: in the dark and pure-black themes it is the only thing that says where one card ends and the other begins. `?colorAccent` is `?aboutScreenColor` in both AppBaseTheme and AppBaseThemeDark, so the ripple is the app's accent blue rather than the platform grey. The four properties are the rule: fill, 2dp stroke, 5dp corners, accent ripple — 6dp of elevation on its own reproduces none of them.
